speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are here because your newborn is having trouble breathing. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they seem worse during feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given the preterm birth at 32 weeks, cesarean section, and maternal gestational diabetes, are you noticing any nasal flaring, grunting, or chest retractions right now? Also, has the baby passed meconium, and if so, was it green or black?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a 32-week preterm infant born via C-section with maternal gestational diabetes, presenting with tachypnea, nasal flaring, grunting, subcostal retractions, and cyanosis, is classic for surfactant deficiency due to prematurity.
